spells.name: Pestilence
spells.description:
A swarm of insects fills the area. Creatures that begin their turn within the spell’s area or who enter the area for the first time on their turn must make a Constitution saving throw or take 1d4 piercing damage. The pests also ravage any unattended organic material within their radius, such as plant, wood, or fabric.

This spell’s damage increases by 1d4 when you reach 5th level (2d4), 10th level (3d4), and 15th level (4d4).

spells.name: Prestidigitation
spells.description:
You wield arcane energies to produce minor effects. Choose one of the following: 

* create a single burst of magic that manifests to one of the senses (for example a burst of sound, sparks, or an odd odor).
* clean or soil an object of 1 cubic foot or less.
* light or snuff a flame.
* chill, warm, or flavor nonliving material of 1 cubic foot or less for 1 hour.
* color or mark an object or surface for 1 hour.
* create an ordinary trinket or illusionary image that fits in your hand and lasts for 1 round.

You may cast this spell multiple times, though only three effects may be active at a time. Dismissing each effect requires an action.

spells.name: Fog Cloud
spells.description:
You create a heavily obscured area of fog. The fog spreads around corners and can be dispersed by a moderate wind (at least 10 miles per hour).

Cast at Higher Levels
The spell’s radius increases by 20 feet for each slot level above 1st.

spells.name: Inflict Wounds
spells.description:
You impart fell energies that suck away the target’s life force, making a melee spell attack that deals 3d10 necrotic damage.

Cast at Higher Levels
The damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 1st.

spells.name: Shadow Armor
spells.description: When attacked to trigger. Attack gets disavantage on the attack. Gain resistance to Radiant damage until end of my turn

spells.name: Elemental Rebound
spells.description:
You redirect and reflect a portion of incoming elemental energy. You gain resistance to the damage type that triggered this spell, which applies against the incoming damage. The next time you deal damage before this spell ends, one of your targets takes 1d6 damage of the triggering type. Dealing this extra damage ends the spell early.

MOAR 222

spells.name: Ice Bolts
spells.description:
You create three bolts of ice that you direct at one or more creatures within range and line of sight. Each bolt hits automatically and does 1d6 cold damage. The bolts all strike simultaneously.

Enhancement: For each spell slot used higher than 1st level, you create one additional bolt.

Book of Lost Spells 73

spells.name: Armor of Agathys
spells.description:
Protective magical frost surrounds you. You gain 5 Temporary Hit Points. If a creature hits you with a melee attack roll before the spell ends, the creature takes 5 Cold damage. The spell ends early if you have no Temporary Hit Points.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The Temporary Hit Points and the Cold damage both increase by 5 for each spell slot level above 1.

spells.name: Ray of Frost
spells.description:
An icy beam shoots from your outstretched fingers. Make a ranged spell attack . On a hit, you deal 1d8 cold damage and reduce the target’s Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

This spell’s damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).

notes.title: Back Story
notes.body_md:
## 

## Torak's Sire: The General (Alaric). 

In life, the General fell to an onslaught of Chernobog's feral vampires (Draugr). They infected him with their curse, but his own burning will and hatred of the undead allowed him to choose his own fate. He spent decades upon decades recruiting the toughest warriors into service. Those who survived his training were given the chance to join the Einherjar.  He hand-picked Torak and, in a ritual out on the tundra and in the heart of a blizzard, drove a shard of starlight ice into the young soldier's chest, replacing his heart with the Frost of the North. 

When Hrimm-Kastel fell, Alaric stayed behind to buy time for the others to flee and brought many traitors down. Their bloody, dying screams followed Torak and his family as they fled to Ironcrag Hold. Torak dreams of his sire wandering the Bleak Expanse, a broken spear with an orange-glowing tip in his hand as he hunts the enemy. 

## The Widow's Nail

The fortress your family controlled along the wall is called Hrimm-Kastjel (Rime Bastion) by the dwarves, but it is also known as the "Widow's Nail" by the human and giant Jarls. It was a human, Jarl Hlothar Kurgensson, who led the betrayal. He was the leader of a settlement near the wall and provided your family with supplies. A rumour of an ancient artifact in the deep dungeons of the fortress caused him to betray you and your family to get at the relic. You never heard any such rumour. 

## The Dwarves

The survivors fled to Ironcrag Hold. The dwarves there, led by Thane Hreidmar "Stone-Eye," are Clan Bofyr. These dwarves referred to your family as "Einherjar," an important distinction. The north has many undead types, especially on the other side of the Wall, but most vampires are feral Darakhul, lowly beasts little better than ghouls. Einherjar are referred to as the Heroic Dead, who gave up Valhalla to continue the fight in the mortal world. 

Thane Stone-Eye, who has a carved sapphire in his left eye socket, is said to be able to see through half-truths and illusions. He is a devout follower of Wotan. 

One final secret: one of the ancestors of Clan Bofyr is a dwarven vampire wizard who was the one who recommended the thane ally with your people. You know of this secret, as it was part of why you trusted the thane. He gave you this secret to prove his loyalty and respect.

The clan is watched over by an Einjerjar, a 1500-year-old vampire named Valdrin Bofyr, Deep-Root of the Mountain, Master of the Old Oaths of Stone and Blood. Valdrin has given Torak a blood oath to protect the remaining members of his family. The elder vampire awoke from torpor when the fortress fell and Alaric was slain. His skin has taken a rough, stone-like texture, and when he slumbers most would mistake him for a statue of a dwarf on a throne in a forgotten chamber high on the mountain.
